words.definition: a group that is smaller in number or has less social or political power than the dominant group
words.japanese: 少数派・マイノリティ
words.example: The policy aims to improve representation of ethnic minorities.

words.definition: a system in which opportunities and rewards are based mainly on ability and achievement
words.example: Supporters argue that exams can promote meritocracy, while critics question equal access.

words.definition: the completion of a course of study, usually marked by a formal ceremony
words.example: Her family travelled to attend her graduation.

words.definition: the act or number of people officially registered in a school or course
words.example: University enrolment increased after tuition support was introduced.

words.definition: the act or record of being present at school, work or an event
words.example: Regular attendance is strongly linked to academic progress.

words.definition: an official document showing that someone has completed a course of study
words.example: She received her diploma at the end of the ceremony.

words.definition: the reason or desire that makes a person act or work toward a goal
words.example: A supportive teacher can increase students’ motivation.

words.definition: the qualifications or conditions needed to be accepted into a course or institution
words.example: Applicants should check the entry requirements before applying.

words.definition: a person who leaves school or a course before completing it
words.example: The programme provides support for students at risk of becoming dropouts.

words.definition: unable to read or write sufficiently
words.example: Adult education programmes support people who are illiterate.

words.definition: designed to include and support people with different backgrounds or needs
words.example: An inclusive classroom gives every student a chance to participate.

words.definition: the ideas, institutions or practices accepted by most people in a society
words.example: The initiative helps minority students enter mainstream education.

words.definition: required by law, rule or authority
words.example: Education is compulsory until a certain age in many countries.

words.definition: policies intended to improve opportunities for groups that have faced historical disadvantage or discrimination
words.example: The university debated the role of affirmative action in admissions.

words.definition: financial support awarded to a student for study, often based on achievement or need
words.example: She received a scholarship that covered most of her tuition fees.

words.definition: to recognise or respond to differences between people, needs or levels
words.japanese: 区別する・差に応じて対応する
words.example: Teachers differentiate tasks so that learners at different levels can succeed.

words.definition: unfair treatment of people because of characteristics such as race, gender or religion
words.example: The law prohibits discrimination in education and employment.

words.definition: the condition in which all people have the same opportunity to use a service or resource
words.japanese: 平等なアクセス・機会
words.example: Reliable internet is important for equal access to online education.

words.definition: unequal access to educational opportunities, resources or outcomes
words.example: Income and location can contribute to educational inequality.

words.definition: the ability of individuals or families to move to a different social or economic position
words.example: Education is often seen as a route to greater social mobility.

words.definition: a system of government in which people choose leaders and influence decisions, usually through elections
words.example: Free elections are a central feature of democracy.

words.definition: a person who works publicly and actively to bring about social or political change
words.example: The activist organised a campaign for equal rights.

words.definition: a system of government in which one ruler or small group holds extensive power with limited public control
words.example: Opposition parties were banned under the dictatorship.

words.definition: the act of formally choosing a candidate or decision in an election or meeting
words.example: The campaign encouraged young adults to take part in voting.

words.definition: a state in which the head of state is not a hereditary monarch and political authority is based on public institutions
words.example: The country became a republic after the monarchy ended.

words.definition: originating among ordinary people in a community rather than from powerful institutions
words.example: A grassroots movement collected thousands of local signatures.

words.definition: a public expression of disagreement or opposition
words.example: Students organised a peaceful protest outside the city hall.

words.definition: general agreement reached by a group after discussion
words.example: The committee struggled to reach consensus on the new rules.

words.definition: the authority of a state to govern itself and control its own affairs
words.example: The treaty raised questions about national sovereignty.

words.definition: a formal written request signed by people who want an authority to take action
words.example: More than ten thousand people signed the petition.

words.definition: a formal process in which people vote to choose political representatives or leaders
words.example: The election will determine the next national government.

words.definition: an organised series of activities designed to achieve a political or social goal
words.example: The campaign focused on increasing voter participation.

words.definition: legal, social or moral entitlements that people are considered to possess
words.example: Citizens protested to defend their voting rights.

words.definition: the condition of having the same rights, status or opportunities
words.example: The organisation campaigns for gender equality.

words.definition: organisations and groups outside government and business through which citizens participate in public life
words.example: A strong civil society can hold governments accountable.

words.definition: rule by a leader who exercises absolute power in a cruel or oppressive way
words.example: The novel portrays a society struggling against despotism.

words.definition: the ability or opportunity to express opinions and influence decisions
words.japanese: 発言権・意見を表す力
words.example: Local councils can give young people a stronger voice in community decisions.

words.definition: a major and often rapid change in a political or social system, sometimes involving force
words.example: The revolution replaced the old political system.

words.definition: an official rule made by a government or authority to control an activity
words.example: New regulation limits the use of personal data by companies.

words.definition: activities through which people influence politics, such as voting, campaigning or protesting
words.example: Schools can teach students why political participation matters.

words.definition: formal promises made during a marriage or other serious commitment
words.example: The couple exchanged vows in front of their families.

words.definition: a strong promise or willingness to devote time and effort to a person, goal or relationship
words.example: A long-term relationship requires commitment from both partners.

words.definition: the legal ending of a marriage
words.example: They decided to divorce after years of disagreement.

words.definition: a marriage in which families or others play a major role in selecting the partners
words.japanese: お見合い結婚・取り決め婚
words.example: The interview compares arranged marriage with individual partner choice.

words.definition: a person’s husband, wife or legally recognised married partner
words.example: Employees may include a spouse on the family insurance plan.

words.definition: a formal event performed according to traditional or official customs
words.example: The wedding ceremony included traditions from both families.

words.definition: a relationship in which two people share responsibilities and support one another
words.example: They see marriage as an equal partnership.

words.definition: a close personal connection involving trust, affection and emotional openness
words.example: Honest communication can strengthen intimacy in a relationship.

words.definition: affection and care that do not depend on specific conditions or behaviour
words.example: The speaker described parental care as unconditional love.

words.definition: spending time with someone in order to develop or explore a romantic relationship
words.example: Online apps have changed how some people approach dating.

words.definition: social expectations about how people should behave based on gender
words.example: Gender roles within families have changed in many societies.

words.definition: a romantic or intimate relationship between people of the same sex
words.japanese: 同性関係・同性カップルの関係
words.example: The law now gives same-sex relationships greater legal recognition.

words.definition: an agreement in which each side accepts less than it originally wanted
words.example: Living together often requires compromise.

words.definition: a relationship in which each person values and considers the other equally
words.example: Mutual respect is essential for a healthy partnership.

words.definition: a close romantic relationship intended or maintained over an extended period
words.example: Trust tends to become especially important in a long-term relationship.

words.definition: to end a romantic relationship
words.example: They split up but remained on friendly terms.

words.definition: relying on another person for financial, emotional or practical support
words.japanese: 依存している・扶養されている
words.example: One partner became financially dependent after leaving work to care for a child.

words.definition: tasks or responsibilities that a person is expected or required to perform
words.example: The couple discussed how to share household duties fairly.

words.definition: the traditional or deliberate process of seeking to develop a romantic relationship before marriage
words.japanese: 求愛・結婚を前提とした交際
words.example: Courting customs differ greatly between cultures.

words.definition: beliefs about how married partners should behave and what marriage should provide
words.example: Different marital expectations can create conflict if couples never discuss them.
